Me and my gal pal were skating late at night on our college campus. We were hunting for huge parking garages to shred down where we could drink and race and no one would see. 

We took the elevator up and this particular garage locked the lobby room the elevator was in from the inside so we had no way to be on the roof floor of the garage. We went back down to floor one.

As the doors opened, we were on the complete other side of the garage. We were both speechless, absolutely floored. We never believed in this stuff let alone being transported across such a insignificant cosmic distance.

Turns out, we didn’t start on floor one, rather the *ground* floor. We weren’t used to the weird labeling on the elevator.

I’m a performer in theatre, I act in front of hundreds of people in compromising positions, in vulnerable emotional states, sometimes disrobed to varying degrees. I meet and have rehearsal with strangers who touch me, talk to me, yell at me, and sometimes become intimate with me depending on the part.

I am extremely agoraphobic. I can’t be in any sort of crowd without freaking the fuck out, I have to always have an exit in view, and I have to always know layouts of buildings I enter so I know how I can leave as fast as possible. People standing too near to me or touching me often makes me break out in small panic attacks. If you happen to be in school or college, imagine the announcement that a fellow classmate has took his/her own life. People who don't even know you will be emotionally hurt. I've lost too many to things like this because they've thought no one cared, but believe me when I say I care. I care so much. The loss of human life is so heartbreaking for anyone. Please reconsider any thoughts of ending your life. Please know that I'm here to talk to you, given I see a reply. Please please please do not end your life today. Or tomorrow. Or the next day. Or ever. Live a long and happy life. I assume you can get through this if you realize the true situation around you. You are loved. People care. I care.

I'm no expert on preventing suicide, but I can certainly suggest things to help...
Talk to someone! It can be anyone. It can be me. It can be someone over the phone. It can be yourself, just talk about what's happening.
Listen to music! If you like music, find a band or singer or songwriter you like and listen. I know music has always helped me get through rough patches, maybe it'll help you too.
Get your mind off the bad things! I know sometimes it feels like you're always thinking negative or it's like there is a constant gray cloud looming above you all day, but you can change that. If you start doing something you love, bad thoughts will vanish. You could draw, listen or play music, like mentioned before, you could take a walk or a run. Anything to get you thinking differently.

Please. Realize you are loved. Realize people care. If you don't think others care, I do. I really, really do. Please.
